THE CASE OF THE "RALPH MOLLER".

Although the "Ralph Moller" incident has been
closed for some time yet certain enquiries which have been
made have proved to be of interest and have elucidated to
a great extent various circumstances which, at the time,
were somewhat puzzling. All the information which has sub-
sequently been received confirms the original report that
the "Ralph Moller" had been fitted out to give assistance
to the Bolsheviks who were hard pressed in Kamchatka, and
has also thrown considerable light upon the dealings of
certain of the leading Bolshevik agents in the Far East.
Certain enquiries were made in Japan and the information
obtained there in addition to that subsequently received
in Shanghai makes up practically a complete story of the
venture.

Little need be said regarding the "Ralph Moller"
herself and her cargo which on examination was found to
consist of large quantities of flour, clothing, tinned food,
hardware, etc. Most of this cargo was stored at Hakodate
when the "Ralph Moller" returned to Shanghai. The passengers
who were on the boat proceeded to Shanghai via Japan not
daring to risk another journey on the "Ralph Moller". It
was ascertained that there was no wireless set on the "Ralph
Moller". Young, the captain of the boat, stated that a pro-
posal had been made in Shanghai to fit the "Ralph Moller"
with a wireless installation which, of course, could easily
have been removed on arrival in Kamchatka, but it was even-
tually decided not to do so. It is probable that it was

“拉尔夫·莫勒”号（"Ralph Moller"）案。

尽管“拉尔夫·莫勒”号事件已结案一段时间，但随后进行的一些调查被证明颇具意义，并在很大程度上阐明了当时令人颇为困惑的各种情况。此后收到的所有信息均证实了最初的报告，即“拉尔夫·莫勒”号经过装备，旨在援助在堪察加（Kamchatka）处境艰难的布尔什维克分子；同时也使人们进一步了解了某些远东主要布尔什维克代理人的活动情况。在日本进行了一些调查，在那里获得的信息加上随后在上海收到的信息，几乎拼凑出了这次冒险行动的完整经过。

关于“拉尔夫·莫勒”号本身及其货物，无需多言。经检查，货物包括大量面粉、衣物、罐头食品、五金器具等。当“拉尔夫·莫勒”号返回上海时，大部分货物仍存放在函馆（Hakodate）。船上的乘客经日本前往上海，不敢再冒险乘坐“拉尔夫·莫勒”号航行。经查实，“拉尔夫·莫勒”号上没有无线电台。该船船长杨（Young）称，曾有人提议在上海为“拉尔夫·莫勒”号安装无线设备，当然，这些设备在抵达堪察加后可以轻易拆除，但最终决定不这样做。这可能是因为考虑到该提议风险太大，因为据查，上海只有一套真正高效的无线设备出售，购买它无疑会引起不良关注。

on board that boat became extremely nervous when questioned
about him. The captain, when interrogated, stated he knew
that Clarke was a close friend of Dorf, and the chief representative, at Shanghai, of the White Government in connection
with Kamchatka affairs. Further that Clarke, at first, intended to sail on the White gunboat the "Admiral Zavoika", but as
a permit for her departure was refused by the Chinese Commissioner for Foreign Affairs in Shanghai this plan fell through.
Subsequently Clarke proposed to sail on the "Ralph Roller"
but this idea also came to nothing. The captain added that
when leaving Shanghai he was ordered to stop at Kosung where
he received a message telling him to call at Muroran to purchase coal. This order he regarded as very mystifying as
although coal might have been somewhat cheaper at Muroran it
certainly would not have been a saving to call at that port
owing to the extra expense entailed by steaming a longer distance. All this mystery regarding Clarke has now been cleared
up by the fact that his identity has been established with
John Paul Grey, and there can be no doubt that the instructions
received regarding the call at Muroran were merely a blind to
cover Clarke joining the ship at that port. Whilst the "Ralph
Roller" was making her way to Muroran Clarke, under the name
of John Paul Grey, was busy trying to obtain a passport at
the British Consulate in Shanghai to enable him to proceed to
Hakodate from where, of course, he could easily reach Muroran
and meet the "Ralph Roller". Gray's written application for

此事的两名主要人物无疑是约翰·克拉克（John Clarke）和尼古拉斯·多尔夫（Nicholas Dorf）。人们会记得，海参崴（Vladivostok）政府认为克拉克在“拉尔夫·莫勒”号（原文误作 "Ralph Roller"）上，当被问及他时，船上的乘客变得极为紧张。船长在接受讯问时表示，他知道克拉克是多尔夫的密友，也是白俄政府在上海负责堪察加事务的主要代表。此外，克拉克起初打算乘坐白俄炮舰“扎沃伊科海军上将”号（"Admiral Zavoika"）航行，但由于上海中国外交专员拒绝签发离境许可，该计划落空。随后克拉克提议乘坐“拉尔夫·莫勒”号（原文误作 "Ralph Roller"），但这一想法也未实现。船长补充说，离开上海时，他奉命在古宋（Kosung，音译）停泊，在那里他收到一条消息，让他停靠室兰（Muroran）购买煤炭。他认为这道命令非常神秘，因为虽然室兰的煤炭可能稍便宜些，但由于需要航行更长的距离而产生额外费用，停靠该港口肯定无法节省开支。如今，随着克拉克的身份被确认为约翰·保罗·格雷（John Paul Grey），所有关于克拉克的谜团都已解开，毫无疑问，有关停靠室兰的指示仅仅是一个幌子，目的是掩盖克拉克在该港口登船的事实。当“拉尔夫·莫勒”号（原文误作 "Ralph Roller"）驶往室兰途中，化名为约翰·保罗·格雷的克拉克正忙于在上海英国领事馆申请护照，以便他能前往函馆，从那里他自然可以轻易到达室兰并与“拉尔夫·莫勒”号会合。格雷的书面护照申请得到了他的朋友尼古拉斯·多尔夫的支持，后者负责“拉尔夫·莫勒”号（原文误作 "Ralph Muller"）上的货物。

terrogated at Muroran Dorf stated that he was the sole owner
of the whole cargo and the passengers were people employed
by him. This statement was completely false as enquiries
have shown that the cargo was purchased by the Centro-Souz
in Shanghai through various agents one of whom, named Sere-
brianikoff, had previously made himself conspicuous in various
shady arms deals. It is interesting to know that great efforts
were made by the persons engaged by the Centro-Souz in pur-
chasing cloth to get the large quantity which they had bought,
carefully matched, the reason for this being that it was wanted
for uniforms for the Bolshevik troops in Kamchatka.

Quite how far everything was entrusted by the Centro-
Souz in Dorf's hands it is hard to say, but it is significant
that when the "Ralph Muller" arrived at Muroran a brother of
A. Kossolapof, the manager of the Centro-Souz, was there to
meet the boat.

The enquiries regarding J. F. Gray and the Clarke
family have been very interesting and were much facilitated
by the action of the Japanese Government in expelling from
Japan, Boris Gray, who, there are good reasons to believe, was
engaged in communist propaganda work in Japan. Boris Gray
after his expulsion from Japan came to Shanghai where he --
stopped at 41, Seymour Road with John Paul Gray who turned out
to be his brother. It is probable that this Boris Gray is
identical with the Gray who was arrested by the Peking author-
ities for having in his possession a large amount of Bolshevik
literature and propaganda. According to Japanese reports Boris
Gray was in close touch with the Japanese Communist agent --
Shijete Yoichi who is usually known as Kono Tetsuo. From the
enquiries made by the Japanese it appears that Boris Gray was
born

在室兰接受讯问时，多尔夫声称他是整批货物的唯一所有者，乘客是他雇佣的人员。这一陈述完全虚假，因为调查显示，这批货物是由中央苏维埃合作社（Centro-Souz）在上海通过各类代理人购买的，其中一名名为谢列布里亚尼科夫（Serebrianikoff）的代理人此前曾在各种可疑的军火交易中崭露头角。值得注意的是，受中央苏维埃合作社雇佣购买布料的人极力设法将他们购买的大量布料仔细配对，原因是这些布料用于制作堪察加布尔什维克军队的制服。

很难说清中央苏维埃合作社在多大程度上将一切事务托付给多尔夫处理，但具有象征意义的是，当“拉尔夫·莫勒”号（原文误作 "Ralph Muller"）抵达室兰时，中央苏维埃合作社经理 A. 科索拉波夫（A. Kossolapof）的兄弟在那里迎接该船。

关于 J. F. 格雷和克拉克家族的调查非常有趣，且得益于日本政府将鲍里斯·格雷（Boris Gray）驱逐出日本的行动而大大便利。有充分理由相信，鲍里斯·格雷在日本从事共产主义宣传工作。鲍里斯·格雷被驱逐出日本后来到上海，与约翰·保罗·格雷同住西摩路（Seymour Road）41号，后者原来是他的兄弟。这位鲍里斯·格雷很可能就是此前因持有大量布尔什维克文献和宣传品而被北京当局逮捕的那个格雷。根据日本方面的报告，鲍里斯·格雷与日本共产党代理人——通常被称为河野铁雄（Kono Tetsuo）的 Shijete Yoichi（音译）——保持密切联系。从日本方面进行的调查来看，鲍里斯·格雷出生于

there went to Australia acquiring British nationality in 1914.
In 1917 he went to Vladivostok and then returned to Australia
where it is stated that he owns a farm at Wallumbilla, Queens-

Inquiries regarding these two brothers have elicited
the fact that they are the sons of a certain Paul Clarke who
originally was an employee in the Baikal Railway and who -
emigrated to Australia in 1915 after having, according to the
Russian Newspapers, served a term of imprisonment. In Austra-
lia Clarke changed his name to Gray. At the outbreak of the
Russian Revolution Paul Clarke returned to Russia under his
own name and became one of the most prominent Bolshevik leaders
in the Far East. At present he is employed at Chita, and -
during the time of the Antonoff Government was Minister of
Transport subsequently representing the Vladivostok Bolsheviks
in the Far Eastern Republican Constituent Assembly. Paul
Clarke has four sons all of whom are said to be active Bolshe-
viks. John Clarke, alias John Paul Gray was, according to the
Russian newspapers, for some time employed by the American Red
Cross at Vladivostok whilst the Kolchak Government was in power.
Subsequently he was elected a member of the Far Eastern Repub-
lican Bureau of Communists and later held the position of a
member of the Primorie National Assembly in which he acted, on
different occasions, as a Secretary, Minister for Home Affairs
and Assistant President of the Cabinet. Subsequently he was
elected a member of the Far Eastern Republican Government and
became one of the five members of the Directorate. As a member
of the Directorate John Clarke was appointed by Moscow as a
Commissary in Kamchatka and proceeded to Shanghai to obtain -
supplies for Kamchatka. John Clarke is still residing in -
Shanghai under the name of John Paul Gray.

关于这两兄弟的调查揭示了一个事实：他们是某位保罗·克拉克（Paul Clarke）的儿子，保罗·克拉克原为贝加尔铁路（Baikal Railway）的员工，据俄国报纸报道，他在服刑期满后于1915年移民澳大利亚。在澳大利亚，克拉克改姓为格雷。俄国革命爆发时，保罗·克拉克恢复原名返回俄国，并成为远东最杰出的布尔什维克领导人之一。目前他在赤塔任职，在安东诺夫（Antonoff）政府时期曾任交通部长，随后在远东共和国制宪会议中代表海参崴布尔什维克。保罗·克拉克有四个儿子，据说都是活跃的布尔什维克分子。据俄国报纸报道，约翰·克拉克（化名约翰·保罗·格雷）在高尔察克（Kolchak）政府掌权期间，曾一度在海参崴受雇于美国红十字会。随后，他当选为远东共和国共产党局成员，后来担任滨海省（Primorie）国民议会议员，在此期间他曾先后担任秘书、内政部长和内阁副总统。随后，他当选为远东共和国政府成员，并成为五人执政团成员之一。作为执政团成员，约翰·克拉克被莫斯科任命为堪察加专员，并前往上海为堪察加获取物资。约翰·克拉克目前仍以约翰·保罗·格雷的名义居住在上海。

The second brother Boris Clarke, alias Boris Gray,
is believed to be the man who arrived in Shanghai on July 6th,
1921, on board the s.s. "Admiral Zavoika" bringing with him a
valuable cargo of furs and skins the sale of which is said to
have brought in about £70,000. After stopping with his brother
Boris Gray left Shanghai for Harbin.

Little is known regarding two other brothers, but
one of them may be a certain Vlademar Gray who in 1917 arrived
in Harbin as a representative of two Labour Papers of Brisbane.
This man was of Russian origin and had been naturalised in -
Australia.

Nicholas Dorf, the close friend of John Clarke, after
being away for some time has recently returned to Shanghai in
company with Ozornin, a well known Bolshevik worker of Harbin.
It is not known, however, what is the reason of his visit to
Shanghai.

It is more than probable that more will be heard of
the Gray family and their friends as, undoubtedly, they are the
people who control the main funds, at Shanghai, of the Far East-
ern Government, and it is probable that through them sums of -
money are sent from Moscow for propaganda in the Far East.
John Clarke, (John Paul Gray) however, is an extremely cautious
person and associates as little as possible with other well-
known Bolshevik workers in Shanghai, so it will not be easy to
follow his movements and ascertain his plans.

第二个兄弟鲍里斯·克拉克（Boris Clarke），化名鲍里斯·格雷，被认为是1921年7月6日乘坐“扎沃伊科海军上将”号轮船抵达上海的人，他带来了一批珍贵的毛皮和皮革货物，据说出售所得约为7万英镑。在与兄弟同住一段时间后，鲍里斯·格雷离开上海前往哈尔滨。

关于另外两个兄弟的情况知之甚少，但其中一人可能是某位弗拉迪马尔·格雷（Vlademar Gray），此人于1917年作为布里斯班两家劳工报纸的代表抵达哈尔滨。此人为俄罗斯裔，已在澳大利亚归化入籍。

约翰·克拉克的密友尼古拉斯·多尔夫在离开一段时间后，最近与哈尔滨著名的布尔什维克工作者奥佐尔宁（Ozornin）一同返回上海。然而，不知他此次访问上海的原因。

极有可能今后还会听到更多关于格雷家族及其朋友的消息，因为毫无疑问，他们是控制着上海远东政府主要资金的人，而且很可能通过他们，莫斯科向远东输送资金用于宣传工作。然而，约翰·克拉克（约翰·保罗·格雷）是一个极其谨慎的人，尽可能少与其他在上海知名的布尔什维克工作者交往，因此要跟踪他的行踪并查明他的计划并非易事。

REPORT ON J. P. Gray and B. Gray

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

Re John Paul Gray and Boris Gray, I am informed that there are a father and four sons in the family and that their real name is Clark. The father is said to have held a good position in the railway service under the Bolsheviks first at Vladivostok and now at Chita. The four sons are also said to be active Bolsheviks. J. P. Gray and his wife are still staying at 41 Seymour Road, Boris Gray has left there having, according to the servants, gone to Harbin, and Mr. and Mrs. Vitoffsky, J. P. Gray's mother-in-law and father-in-law who formerly also stayed at 41 Seymour Road have removed to 389 Avenue Joffre. Vitoffsky is advertising in the "Russian Echo" as a teacher who requires Russian pupils so as to start a Russian school. Boris Gray is stated to be the man who disposed of about $70,000.00 worth of furs and skins which were brought to Shanghai on board the s.s. "Admiral Zavoika" on July 6, 1921. The proceeds of the sale of the furs are said to have been either sent to the Chita Government or used by Gray on their behalf. There is no doubt that there are two men, J. P. Gray and Boris Gray as the former was living at 41 Seymour Road whilst the latter occupied room No. 14 at the Savoy Hotel from November 1 to November 14, 1921. There is also no doubt that J. P. Gray was staying at 41 Seymour Road at the time Boris Gray was being deported from Japan.

All the family are stated to be known as both Gray and Clark.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature]

D. G. I.

THE JAPAN WEEKLY CHRONICLE. [December 8th, 1921]

MANY UNDER ARREST.
ALLEGED SOVIET PROPAGANDA.

The Mainichi says that the examination of many Socialists by the Metropolitan Police and others has revealed the fact that there exists in Tokyo a secret society called the Tokyo Communist Party, and that this organisation was the head and front of the recent Socialist movement, which was conceived on a very extensive scale. Among the documents seized as the result of a domiciliary search made in the house of Kondo Eizo, a member of the Balbunsha, was a manifesto issued by the Tokyo Communist Party. This secret society, it is alleged, was brought into being for the express purpose of Bolshevising Japan, and has been working in concert with the Propaganda department of the Soviet Government, the propaganda expenses being furnished by the Shanghai branch of the Soviet Propaganda Department.

With regard to Mr. B. Grey, who is under police suspicion, it has been made clear by statements made by Yamagami Masayoshi and Kondo Eizo, now under arrest, that the real object of his present visit to Japan is for the purpose of supplying the necessary funds to the Japanese association. It is said that although Mr. Grey denies the accusation, saying that the object of his present visit is for the purpose of purchasing medical instruments for the Chemical and Medical Company in Shanghai, inquiries made by the Japanese authorities at Shanghai showed that he was telling an untruth. On the afternoon of the 28th ultimo, two high police officers of the Metropolitan Police proceeded to Yokohama and examined him at the Kagacho Police Station.

Kondo Eizo has been formally prosecuted on the charge of violating the national constitution.

MR. GREY DEPORTED.

A deportation order from the Home Minister was served on Mr. B. Grey on the 2nd inst. The order is that he should leave Japanese territory within a week. It is alleged in the Japanese papers that the close examination of the foreigner which has been carried out by the police authorities has established the fact that he has come to Japan on the mission of propagating Bolshevism in Japan, acting under instructions from the Soviet Government.

FRUITFUL SOIL.

North Kyushu, which embraces the coalmining and industrial centres, is evidently regarded by Socialists and other "ists" as a fruitful field for propaganda, or else the local authorities are specially nervous, for news comes from time to time from that quarter of campaigns there. The latest is telegraphed to the Mainichi from Omuda. This message says that news of the arrival at Omuda, Fukuoka prefecture, of Yoneda Kozo, a Kobe Socialist, and six other Socialists, coming to the ears of the police, strict vigilance was being exercised, when the local police got hold of the information that the Hara Printing Office of the city was turning out propaganda literature for the visiting Socialists. On the afternoon of the 30th ultimo at about 3 o'clock Saito Satoru, one of the Socialistic band, fell into the hands of the police, who were lying in ambush, when he was leaving the printing office with 2,000 seditious handbills. The prisoner was being taken to the local police station by five policemen, when the party came across a procession of townsfolk who were escorting a new recruit to the barracks. Saito straightway began to distribute broadcast the printed matter. The police had been taken unawares, and before the man could be stopped he succeeded in disseminating many of the bills. Together with some others, he is now undergoing examination.

It is said that this bill was signed by "The Kyushu Proletariat League," and urges in strong terms the destruction of the capitalist system.

POLICE STATEMENT CONCERNING MR. GREY.

REASONS FOR DEPORTATION.

Mr Otsuka, the Chief of the Foreign Section of the Police Bureau of the Home Office, published the following statement with regard to Mr. Grey, who has been served with a deportation order:—

"Grey was born in Moscow. Thirteen years ago he went to Chita, where he married a Russian and had two children. For some years after 1909 he was farming in Australia, and in 1914 he acquired British nationality. In 1917 he proceeded to Vladivostok, and was engaged in mining. In this business he failed, and the following year he went back to Australia. Towards the end of June last year, he obtained a passport from the Melbourne Government, and arrived at Moji on August 26th of the same year by the N.Y.K. steamer Akimaru, travelling via Hongkong and Nagasaki. Two days later he left Tsuruga for Vladivostok. For some time he was doing business between Harbin and Nikolsk. In May last he went to Chita, where he stayed for about six months. During his sojourn there sprang up an intimate relationship between him and Bolsheviks in that district. On October 20th, he got his passport vised by the Chita Government and the local Chinese Consul, and left there for Shanghai via Manchuli, Harbin and Tientsin.

"At Shanghai he was working with the Bolsheviks. When he was there a Japanese named Shigeta Yoichi, under the assumed name of Kono Tetsuo, visited Shanghai as an emissary of the Japan Communist Party, and applied to the Shanghai branch of the Russian Communist Propaganda Department for funds necessary for propaganda in Japan. Grey was then introduced to Shigeta for the first time. It was arranged that the propaganda fund should be handed to the headquarters of the Japan Communist Party by Grey personally, and both of them, Grey and Shigeta, embarked on the Yawata-maru at Shanghai on November 18th for Japan. They landed at Nagasaki two days later, and put up at the Marukin Hotel at Kabashima-cho. Resuming their journey the following morning, Grey arrived at Yokohama on the 22nd ultimo by train, putting up at the Oriental Palace Hotel. As for Shigeta, he parted company with Grey at Yokohama and returned to Tokyo. By this time, the Japanese authorities had been informed of what was going on, and Shigeta was arrested by the police when he visited Grey at the hotel on the 24th. Grey was also taken into police custody and examined. On examination it was discovered that he was in possession of a cheque for ¥5,000 issued by the Shanghai branch of the Bank of Formosa to be cashed at the Yokohama branch of the bank, ¥2,500 in cash, name-cards bearing the emblem of the Russian Communists, and a note-book with the entry of the names of five Japanese Socialists. Shigeta, when examined by the police, made a clean breast of the matter, and this led to Grey's confession of the above-mentioned facts. Grey was also in possession of a brief English code telegram.

"Study was made of the point how Grey stands under Japanese law, and it was found his conduct does not come under the purview of the Japanese law now in force, and consequently it was decided that he should be deported on the ground that his presence in this country is inimical to public peace and order. Shigeta Koichi, who is 28 years old, is a native of Kimitzu-gun, Chiba prefecture. In 1915 he studied at the Waseda University. In 1919 he embraced Socialism, and since that time he has been exerting himself for the establishment of the Japan Communist Party. His present residence is at Kamejimacho, Nihonbashi, Tokyo. He is a consumptive."

It was expected that Mr. Grey, who has been ordered to leave Japan, will probably sail for Shanghai on board the N.Y.K. steamer Kashima-maru, which was to leave Yokohama on the 4th instant at 10 o'clock.

Mr. Oka, the Chief of the Metropolitan Police, was summoned to a Cabinet Council on the 2nd instant to report on the progress of the police activities, now proceeding, and particulars of the case are under investigation.

MORE ARRESTS.

The police investigations of the alleged Socialist propaganda are being pushed on more vigorously than ever, and on the 1st instant the houses of two well-known Socialist leaders, Messrs. Sakai and Toshihiko and Yamagawa Kin, were searched, and documents seized as the result. In addition, searches were made on the same day of the houses of many other Socialists in Tokyo.

As already reported, Kondo Eizo, of the Balbunsha, was formally prosecuted a few days ago on the charge of a violation of the national Constitution. Two other Socialists, Kawasaki Kenjiro and Urata Takeo, were also prosecuted on the same charge, and sent to Tokyo Prison for detention. As a result of domiciliary searches made on the 1st instant eleven other Socialists are said to have been arrested, all being sent to the Procurators' Office of the Tokyo Chiho Saibansho the same night. Those arrested include Arai Kuninosuke and Sano Kizdo, of the Bunkwa-kai (Cultural Society), Karasawa Takunosuke and Hasegawa Tatsujl, of the Rodo-sha (Labourers' Society) and Nakasone Genwa and Yamagami Masayoshi, of the Musan-sha (Proletariat Society).

According to the Asahi, the complicity of Messrs. Sakai and Yamakawa, whose houses were searched on the 1st instant, has become clear, and it is expected that they will shortly be summoned to the Tokyo Court and examined.

The Jiji says that Takao Heibei and Takase Kiyoshi, who are among the Socialists under police suspicion, being in Siberia now for the purpose of attending a meeting of the Third International, the Metropolitan Police have dispatched ten detectives to that region to take them into custody and bring them home.

《日本纪事周刊》。[1921年12月8日]

多人被捕。
涉嫌苏维埃宣传。

《每日新闻》称，警视厅等机构对多名社会主义者进行的审讯揭示了一个事实：东京存在一个名为“东京共产党”的秘密社团，该组织是近期规模宏大的社会主义运动的发起者和核心。在对巴尔本社（Balbunsha）成员近藤荣三（Kondo Eizo）的住所进行搜查时，查获的文件中包括一份由东京共产党发布的宣言。据称，建立这个秘密社团的明确目的是使日本布尔什维克化，其一直与苏维埃政府宣传部协同工作，宣传费用由苏维埃宣传部上海分部提供。

关于受到警方怀疑的 B. 格雷先生，目前被逮捕的山上正义（Yamagami Masayoshi）和近藤荣三的供词已查明，他此次访问日本的真实目的是向该日本协会提供必要资金。据说，尽管格雷先生否认这一指控，声称他此次访问的目的是为上海的化学医药公司购买医疗器械，但日本当局在上海进行的调查显示他在撒谎。上月28日下午，警视厅的两名高级警官前往横滨，在加贺町警察署对他进行了审讯。

近藤荣三因违反国家宪法罪被正式起诉。

格雷先生被驱逐出境。

内务大臣签发的驱逐令已于本月2日送达 B. 格雷先生。命令要求他在一周内离开日本领土。日本报纸称，警方当局对外国人进行的严密调查已证实这样一个事实：他是奉苏维埃政府的指示，肩负着在日本传播布尔什维主义的使命来到日本的。

肥沃的土壤。

北九州涵盖煤矿和工业中心，显然被社会主义者和其他各种“主义者”视为宣传的肥沃领域，否则就是地方当局特别紧张，因为不时有来自该地区的运动消息传来。最新的消息是从大牟田（Omuda）电告《每日新闻》的。这条消息说，神户社会主义者米田耕造（Yoneda Kozo）和其他六名社会主义者抵达福冈县大牟田的消息被警方获悉后，警方加强了严密监视，随后当地警方掌握情报，称市内的原印刷所正在为来访的社会主义者印制宣传刊物。上月30日下午3点左右，社会主义团伙成员之一的斋藤悟（Saito Satoru）在离开印刷所并携带2,000份煽动性传单时，落入了埋伏的警察手中。五名警察正将囚犯押往当地警察署，途中遇到一群护送新兵去兵营的市民队伍。斋藤随即开始四处散发印刷品。警方措手不及，在该男子被制止之前，他成功散发了许多传单。他目前正与其他一些人一起接受审讯。

据说这份传单由“九州无产阶级联盟”签署，并强烈呼吁摧毁资本主义制度。

警方关于格雷先生的声明。

驱逐原因。

内务省警察局外事课长大冢先生就已被送达驱逐令的格雷先生发表了如下声明：—

“格雷出生于莫斯科。十三年前他前往赤塔，在那里娶了一位俄罗斯妻子并育有两个孩子。1909年之后的几年里，他在澳大利亚务农，并于1914年取得英国国籍。1917年他前往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），从事采矿业。这项生意失败了，次年他返回澳大利亚。去年6月底，他从墨尔本政府获得护照，并于同年8月26日乘坐日本邮船会社的‘秋丸’号轮船，经香港和长崎抵达门司。两天后，他离开敦贺前往符拉迪沃斯托克。有一段时间，他在哈尔滨和尼科尔斯克之间做生意。去年5月，他前往赤塔，在那里停留了大约六个月。在此期间，他与该地区的布尔什维克建立了密切关系。10月20日，他的护照获得了赤塔政府和当地中国领事的签证，随后经满洲里、哈尔滨和天津前往上海。

“在上海，他与布尔什维克一起工作。当时，一位名叫重田洋一（Shigeta Yoichi）的日本人化名河野铁雄（Kono Tetsuo），作为日本共产党的使者访问上海，并向俄国共产主义宣传部上海分部申请在日本进行宣传所需的资金。格雷当时首次被介绍给重田。双方商定，宣传资金由格雷亲自交给日本共产党总部，格雷和重田两人于11月18日在上海登上‘八幡丸’号前往日本。两天后他们在长崎登陆，并入住蒲岛町的丸金旅馆。次日早晨继续行程，格雷于上月22日乘火车抵达横滨，入住东方宫殿酒店。至于重田，他在横滨与格雷分手，返回东京。此时，日本当局已获悉事态进展，24日重田到酒店拜访格雷时被警察逮捕。格雷也被警方拘留并接受审讯。经查，发现他持有一张由台湾银行上海分行签发、可在该行横滨分行兑现的5,000日元支票，现金2,500日元，印有俄国共产党人徽章的名片，以及一本记有五名日本社会主义者姓名的笔记本。重田在接受警方审讯时彻底坦白了此事，这导致格雷承认了上述事实。格雷还拥有一份简短的英文密码电报。

“研究了格雷在日本法律下的地位问题，发现其行为不属于现行日本法律的管辖范围，因此决定以他在这个国家的存在有害于公共和平与秩序为由将其驱逐。重田浩一（Shigeta Koichi），28岁，千叶县君津郡人。1915年就读于早稻田大学。1919年信奉社会主义，此后一直致力于建立日本共产党。他目前的住址是东京日本桥龟岛町。他患有肺结核。”

预计已被勒令离开日本的格雷先生可能会乘坐日本邮船会社的‘鹿岛丸’号轮船前往上海，该船定于本月4日上午10点离开横滨。

警视总监冈先生于本月2日被召至内阁会议，汇报目前正在进行的警务活动进展，案件详情正在调查中。

更多逮捕行动。

警方对涉嫌社会主义宣传的调查比以往任何时候都更加 vigorously 推进，本月1日，警方搜查了两名著名社会主义领袖坂井利彦（Sakai Toshihiko）和山川均（Yamakawa Kin）的住所，并查获了文件。此外，当天还搜查了东京许多其他社会主义者的住所。

如前所述，巴尔本社的近藤荣祖几天前因违反国家宪法罪被正式起诉。另外两名社会主义者川崎健次郎（Kawasaki Kenjiro）和浦田武夫（Urata Takeo）也因同一罪名被起诉，并被送往东京监狱拘押。据称，由于本月1日进行的住所搜查，另有11名社会主义者被捕，并于当晚全部被送往东京地方法院检察官办公室。被捕者包括文化协会（Bunkwa-kai）的新井国之助（Arai Kuninosuke）和佐野木堂（Sano Kizdo，音译），劳动者协会（Rodo-sha）的唐泽卓之助（Karasawa Takunosuke）和长谷龙二（Hasegawa Tatsujl，原文如此），以及无产协会（Musan-sha）的中元玄和（Nakasone Genwa）和山上正义（Yamagami Masayoshi）。

据《朝日新闻》报道，本月1日住所被搜查的坂井先生和山川先生的共谋关系已变得清晰，预计他们不久将被传唤至东京法院接受审讯。

《时事新报》称，高尾平兵卫（Takao Heibei）和高濑清（Takase Kiyoshi）等受警方怀疑的社会主义者目前正在西伯利亚参加第三国际会议，警视厅已派遣十名侦探前往该地区将他们逮捕并带回国内。

先生：

SOCIALIST SCARES.
FOREIGNER PESTERED.

It is reported that the Metropolitan Police have finally been able to trace to its source the Socialist propaganda, which it was recently announced had been nipped in the bud. Kondo Eizo and Fujioka Jun, of the Bribunsha, a group of Tokyo Socialists, and other Socialists have been arrested, their houses being searched, and documents seized. It is even reported that a foreigner is suspected as being in the background of the "plot." This foreigner is, according to the Japanese papers, an Englishman named B. Grey, who was born in Russia. He was examined by the Yokohama police at the Grand Oriental Hotel, where he was staying. He absolutely denies having any connection with the Socialist movement, and declares that his present visit to Japan is purely on business. It seems that the police suspect this foreigner of furnishing the Japanese Socialists with money for printing, which, as it was being turned out in large quantities, must have cost a good sum.

The foreign gentleman is quoted by the Asahi as stating that, although he is interested in the study of Communist ideas, nothing is wider of the mark than to accuse him, as the Japanese Police do, of having come to Japan with the object of propagating those ideas or providing money for their propagation. Such propaganda among lower-class Japanese is indeed an impossibility so far as he is concerned, for although the Japanese intellectuals understand English the lower-class people do not. Moreover, he has not a single acquaintance in this country. On his landing at Nagasaki on the 20th inst. he had an interview with a Japanese gentleman, a fact which he thinks had brought him under police suspicion. But as a matter of fact he had no previous acquaintance with the gentleman in question. He further remarks that he has long been studying social conditions in Japan, and is specially interested in the conditions prevailing in this country in the feudal days. As regards the police attentions of which he is now the object, he says that he is not greatly excited; he regards policemen shadowing him as a protection. Their presence about him may serve to keep thieves away. The only difficulty which he experiences on that account is that his commercial transactions, which are his chief object in Japan, are interfered with. According to the same paper, he was to visit Kobe yesterday and leave for Shanghai by a steamer sailing today.

The Asahi says that the police examination of the Socialists now under detention on suspicion of their implication in the recent propaganda movement revealed the fact that two Socialists, Tokuda Kyuichi and Takase Kiyoshi, had left for China and Moscow via Shanghai partly for the purpose of attending the seventh general meeting of the Third International at Irkutsk. Mr. B. Grey, the foreigner under police suspicion, absolutely denies his acquaintance with these and other Japanese Socialists.

Grey 的英国人，出生于俄罗斯。他在横滨的大东方饭店（Grand Oriental Hotel）接受警方讯问，当时他正住在那里。他坚决否认与社会主义运动有任何关联，并声明此次访日纯属商务目的。看来，警方怀疑这名外国人为日本社会主义者提供了印刷资金，鉴于印刷品数量巨大，这必然花费了一大笔钱。

据《朝日新闻》引述，这位外国绅士表示，虽然他对研究共产主义思想感兴趣，但像日本警方那样指责他来到日本的目的是传播这些思想或提供传播资金，完全是无稽之谈。就他而言，在日本下层民众中进行此类宣传确实是不可能的，因为虽然日本知识分子懂英语，但下层民众并不懂。此外，他在该国没有一个熟人。本月20日他在长崎登陆时，曾与一位日本绅士会面，他认为这一事实引起了警方的怀疑。但事实上，他此前并不认识这位绅士。他还评论说，他长期研究日本的社会状况，特别感兴趣的是该国封建时代的状况。至于目前成为警方关注对象一事，他表示并不十分激动；他将跟踪他的警察视为一种保护。他们在他周围出现或许可以起到防盗的作用。他因此遇到的唯一困难是，他的商业交易——这也是他在日本的主要目的——受到了干扰。据同一家报纸报道，他计划昨天访问神户，并于今天乘轮船离开前往上海。

《朝日新闻》称，警方对因涉嫌参与近期宣传运动而被拘留的社会主义者的审讯揭示了一个事实：两名社会主义者德田球一（Tokuda Kyuichi）和高濑清（Takase Kiyoshi）经上海前往中国和莫斯科，部分目的是为了参加在伊尔库茨克举行的第三国际第七次代表大会。受到警方怀疑的外国人 B. Grey 先生坚决否认认识这些日本社会主义者及其他人士。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, DECEMBER 8, 1921.

STRANGE AFFAIR

Visitor From Shanghai
Arrested In Yokohama

Yokohama, Nov. 30.
Mr. Boris Grey, who is said to be of Russian descent but naturalized as a British subject, is being held by the police in Yokohama until they have completed an investigation into alleged Socialist activites among the Japanese. Mr. Grey went to Yokohama from Shanghai on November 25 and registered at one of the leading hotels there. Frequent visits to homes of prominent Socialists in Yokohama and return visits paid him at the hotel are said to have aroused the suspicions of the Japanese police who requested Mr. Grey to report to police headquarters for examination. Mr. Grey is reported to have spent considerable time in Moscow and in Chita before coming to Japan.
The Metropolitan Police are co-operating with the Yokohama authorities in investigating Mr. Grey's object in coming to Japan. The Japanese authorities are inclined to think that there is a connection between him and the recent distribution of inflammatory handbills for the circulation of which several leading Japanese Socialists in many cities have been arrested. Mr. Grey, it is thought, will be brought to Tokyo for further questioning.
Although the Japanese newspapers say that police have evidence that he has a huge fund for propaganda work with which to Bolshevize Japan, the suspected man denies any such intent, insisting that he came to Japan as a commercial traveller representing a wholesale drug firm in Shanghai. Mr. Grey denies having handed money over to anyone as the Japanese newspapers charge.
Mr. Grey had expected to leave Yokohama for Kobe Monday and then to go to Shanghai.
The police here late yesterday declared that they had discovered that the handbills distributed throughout Japan were sent from the headquarters of a secret association of Communists in Tokyo. E. Kondo, K. Kawasaki and several others prominent in local Socialistic ranks have been sent to prison, charged with violating the constitution.—"Japan Advertiser."

横滨，11月30日。
据称具有俄罗斯血统但已归化为英国臣民的 Boris Grey 先生，目前被横滨警方扣留，直到他们完成对涉嫌在日本进行的社会主义活动的调查。Grey 先生于11月25日从上海前往横滨，并在当地一家主要酒店登记入住。据说他频繁拜访横滨著名社会主义者的住所，而这些人士也回访他在酒店的住处，这引起了日本警方的怀疑，警方要求 Grey 先生前往警察总部接受讯问。据报道，Grey 先生在来日本之前，曾在莫斯科和赤塔度过相当长的时间。
大都会警察厅正与横滨当局合作，调查 Grey 先生来日的目的。日本当局倾向于认为他与近期煽动性传单的散发有关，因散发这些传单，多个城市的几名日本主要社会主义者已被逮捕。人们认为 Grey 先生将被带到东京接受进一步讯问。

Confession of Grey, a British subject, who

Five thousand yen from Communist

Mr. Otsuka, the Director of the Police Bureau in
the Home Department, has made the following announcement
in connection with B. Grey :-

"Porlspower Grey was born in Moscow and is a
naturalised British subject. He emigrated to Chita 13
years ago, married a Russian woman named Anna there,
and has had two children.

"He started farming in 1909 in Austria. He
became naturalised in Great Britain in 1914 and in
1917 went to Vladivostock where he engaged in gold
mining, but failed. He went to Australia in 1918.
He obtained a passport from the Melbourne Government at
the end of June, 1920, and left for Japan the following
month by the s.s. "Aki Maru". He arrived at Moji on
August 26, 1920, via Hongkong and Nagasaki, and left
for Vladivostock on August 28 via Tsuruga. He travelled
between Harbin and Nicolsk. He left Vladivostock in
April 1921 for Chita where he arrived in May, and
stayed there about half a year. While there he was
connected with the Bolsheviks. On October 30, he
obtained a passport from the Chita Government, vised by
the Chinese Consul and came to Shanghai via Manchuria
Harbin and Tientsin.

"He was introduced to a Japanese subject named
Yoichi Shigeta who under the assumed name of Torpu Kono
had come to Shanghai as a messenger of the Japanese

来自上海共产党的五千日元。

“他于1909年在奥地利开始从事农业。他于1914年归化为英国公民，并于1917年前往海参崴从事采金业，但以失败告终。他于1918年前往澳大利亚。他于1920年6月底从墨尔本政府获得护照，并于次月乘‘秋丸’号轮船前往日本。他经香港和长崎于1920年8月26日抵达门司，并于8月28日经敦贺前往海参崴。他在哈尔滨和尼科尔斯克（Nicolsk）之间往来。他于1921年4月离开海参崴前往赤塔，5月抵达，并在那里停留了约半年。在此期间，他与布尔什维克有联系。10月30日，他获得了由中国领事签证的赤塔政府护照，经满洲、哈尔滨和天津来到上海。

“他被介绍给一位名为重田洋一（Yoichi Shigeta）的日本臣民，此人化名托普·科诺（Torpu Kono），作为日本共产党

MEMORANDUM - 1.

JOHN P. GRAY.

This man arrived in Shanghai on September 10, 1921
by the s.s. "Sakaki Maru" from Dairen and put up at
the Palace Hotel, occupying room No. 319. On October
2 he removed to No. 41 Seymour Road, a house which he
rented from a Chinese. The persons living at No. 41
Seymour Road are Mr. and Mrs. John P. Gray and their
two children, Mr. and Mrs Vitoffskys and two Misses
Vitoffskys, uncle and aunt and two cousins of Mrs.
John P. Gray and an Australian girl named Ruby Johnson
who is employed as nurse maid to Mrs. Gray's children.
Gray is a Russian who became a naturalised British
subject in Australia. His wife and the Vitoffskys are
Polish. He is not engaged in any business and lives
very quietly. During his stay at the Palace Hotel
it was not noticed that anyone in particular visited
him. So far as can be ascertained he is not associating
with any of the known local supporters of Bolshevism,
but he may have a purpose in keeping apart from them.
It has not, so far, been possible definitely connect
him with the Gray whose luggage was searched in Peking
but enquiries are being continued in this connexion.

Cantonese who resides at 252 Ziang Nyou Lee

clerk and bookkeeper by O. Thoresen, Norwegian
Merchants and Steamship Agents, 9 Avenue Edward
VII for some years. In August last he left

Thoreson's firm leaving a relative named Tsao
( ) to take his place as shipping clerk at

National Labour Union whose headquarters are
at No. 133 Range Road. This society was formed
in August 1919 and the membership is chiefly

business questions. The president is Hoh Shou
Hua ( ), Managing Director of the Yu Vah
Iron Mining Company ( ), 36 Canton Road and
a member of the committee of the Chinese General
Chamber of Commerce. There is no Chinese society
with headquarters in or near the Old German Post
Office but Mahamed Daud & Company where Kiang was
formerly employed and where Tsao is now employed
is in the old German Post Office.

关于 Y. C. Kiang 的报告

由 D. I. Sullivan 撰写    经刑事情报处处长转呈

先生：

Kaung Yih Tsz（江液池），又名 Y. C. Kiang，系广东人，居住于海宁路祥原里252号。他曾在爱德华七世路9号的挪威商人和轮船代理 O. Thoresen 处受雇为职员兼簿记员数年。去年八月，他离开 Thoreson，进入福州路6号的茶叶和皮货进出口商 Mahamed Daud & Co. 任职。他于10月1日离开 Mohamed Daud & Co.，回到 Thoresen 的公司，并留下一位名为 Tsiao（趙）的亲属接替他在 Mahamed Daud 公司担任航运职员的职务。

他是名为“全国劳工联合会”（National Labour Union）的社团成员，该会总部设在兰路133号。该社团成立于1919年8月，会员主要由广东籍店主和商人组成。该会活动非常低调，主要关注商业问题。会长是霍守華（Hoh Shou Hwa），他是广东路36号裕繁铁矿公司（Yu Vah Iron Mining Co.）的董事总经理，也是上海总商会委员会的成员。在旧德国邮局内或附近没有以华人为主体的社团总部，但 Kiang 曾受雇且 Tsiao 现受雇的 Mahamed Daud & Co. 位于旧德国邮局内。

先生，
您忠实的仆人，

Dear Sirs,

The following may be of interest in
connection with today's meeting at the Consulate:

① J. P. Gray. Peking wire not identified
with J.P. Gray of Vladivostok. Dunham suggests
"not" may have been inserted in error,
& wonders if it would be possible to
obtain confirmation of identity locally —
also details as to what Gray is doing?

② FELS, a Pole, takes great interest in
Siberian politics. Living at 31, Borne Road.
Recently arrived from Vladivostok, which he
says is completely controlled by Japanese
through the medium of the new Puppet Govt.
The people of the Coastal Province are
bitterly opposed to Japanese occupation, &
have formed a wide-spread Society named
"Our Russia." There are members throughout
Siberia, their object being the expulsion of
the Japanese. Should the Bolsheviks look
like being able to effect this the Society will
assist them.

③ Y.C. Kiang, a young Chinese employed
by O. Thoresen in the French Concession
states that a new Labour Society (with a
membership of nearly a thousand) which
has its office near the old German Post
Office has recently decided to subscribe to
the resolutions of the Third International.
The Secretary is named TSIAO; he is
endeavouring to make the Society anti-
Japanese. It is apparently controlled
by the Cantonese.

Yours sincerely,
[Signature]

尊敬的先生们：

以下信息可能与今日在领事馆举行的会议有关，谨供参考：

① J. P. Gray。北京来电称其身份与海参崴的 J.P. Gray 不符。Dunham 建议“不（not）”字可能是误植，并想知道是否有可能在当地确认其身份——以及了解 Gray 正在做什么的详细情况？

② FELS，波兰人，对西伯利亚政治极感兴趣。居住在伯恩路31号。最近从海参崴抵达，他说海参崴完全通过新的傀儡政府被日本人控制。滨海省的人民强烈反对日本占领，并组建了一个名为“我们的俄罗斯”（Our Russia）的广泛社团。在西伯利亚各地均有成员，其目标是驱逐日本人。如果布尔什维克看起来能够实现这一目标，该社团将协助他们。

③ Y.C. Kiang，一名在法租界受雇于 O. Thoresen 的年轻华人表示，一个新的劳工社团（拥有近一千名会员），其办事处位于旧德国邮局附近，最近决定拥护第三国际的决议。秘书名为 TSIAO；他正努力使该社团成为反日团体。该社团显然由广东人控制。

此致，
[签名]
